description.narrative: This opportunity originates from the 4th annual call for proposals of its kind since 2021 published by the Flemish Government of through its international climate programme, the Global Substainable Technology and Innovation Community (GSTIC). The programme aimsto support the implementation of Flemish initiatives aimed at combating climate change through demonstration, dissemination and/orcapacity-building projects carried out in developing countries and led by a Flemish company/organisation. The Niger Country Officehas been interested in this opportunity since its 2nd call for proposals in 2022, but was only able to submit a proposal during theproposal during the 3rd call in 2023. Unfortunately, this proposal received a positive response from thedonor. Feedback on the strengths and weaknesses of the proposal was shared with the GSTIC. This feedback was invaluable and committed Oxfam in Niger and OxfamBelgium to revise the proposal with a view to re-submitting it in the 4th call. Niger is oneof the countries most vulnerable to climate change. Temperatures are rising 1.5 times faster in the Sahel than the global average, and climatic phenomena such as droughts and floods are becoming more frequent and severe, disproportionately affecting poorrural populations. The number of floods almost doubled between 2015 and 2020. Rapid soil degradation amplifies climate shocks: it is estimated that 100,000 hectares are lost everyyear to desertification. This puts additional pressure on natural resources,particularly the agricultural sector, exacerbating foodinsecurity and contributing to the vulnerability of populations. This project, which will be implemented by Oxfam in Niger and its partner ANDD Garkua, will be carried out in 4 communes in theZinder Region, including Matameye, Dogo Dogo, Gouchi and Dakoussa, and will focus on implementing actions aimed at strengthening the capacity to adapt to climate change by improving the resilience of communities in the 4 communes in the Zinder Region. Toachieve this, the project will focus on securing the communities' main source of subsistence, agriculture, as well as diversifying their sources of income, and setting up a strategic framework at local level that takes into account the fight against climate change. This will be done through the promotion and adoption of cultivation techniques adapted to the context of climate change on the one hand, and the creation of conditions for the development of income diversification opportunities on the other. In order to root its actions, the second component of the project is working to ensure that, in aparticipatory and inclusive manner, development planning frameworks (PDC, PIA) at local level are updated to include actions and resources to support community actions to combat climate change.

participating-org.narrative: The Nigerien Association for Sustainable Development (ANDD Garkua) is a Nigerien non-profit, non-political and non-confessional NGOcreated by Order n ° 0154 / MISPD / ACR / DGAPJ / DLP of 24 February 2016. Garkua is present in six of the eight regions of Niger. It aims to promote the rights of grassroots communities.
